newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks open lower on weaker exporters.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks open lower on weaker exporters.

text.p: Tokyo stocks dropped in early trade on Wednesday, as blue-chip exporters, especially in the high-technology and automobile sectors, were weighed down by the yen's recent strength against the dollar, brokers said.

At 0013 GMT, the 225-share Nikkei average had lost 139.81 points, or 0.69 percent, to trade at 20,193.02. Nikkei June futures were down 140 points at 20,190. "As the yen has surged so quickly, people want to see when it stabilises, and the cautious stance will cap any rise in blue-chip issues for a while," said a broker at a "Big Four" brokerage house.
"Investor interest has been shifting to issues linked with domestic demand and to lower-priced issues from high-priced blue-chips," said a broker at a second-tier securities house.
